Users who regularly use ChatGPT for quick image searches can now use a brand-new gesture to add photos to a conversation even faster. Let's take a look at how to use it.

ChatGPT makes it easier for users to add just-taken photos to a conversation

Although iOS's Visual Intelligence feature has been available for nearly two years, it currently only supports newer iPhone models and is not available in all regions.

For users who rely on ChatGPT for similar visual searches, attaching an image in the past required tapping the "+" button, selecting "Photos," and then choosing the appropriate image from the album.

Although the process is not overly complicated, this week OpenAI has slightly simplified the steps. Users can now add their most recent photos to a conversation with a convenient new gesture.

OpenAI's Adam Fry stated on the X platform that users can now long-press the "+" button on the left side of the input field to instantly pull up their four most recently taken photos.

Users can select one of these photos to add to the conversation, then ask a question or incorporate it into the prompt content.

This new gesture is one of several improvements ChatGPT has made this week. Other updates include more accurate handling of the current time, improved loading and execution speeds for long conversations on the web version, and clearer interface prompts when users are waiting for a network connection.

Have you ever used AI for visual searches? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
